Set CDC Locator API credentials

Source: R/auth.R
cdc_locator_set_credentials.Rd

Sets the CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID and CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN environment variables for the current R session, so the other functions can find them, and, if you ask, saves them in your .Renviron file for later sessions. The values are never printed.

Usage

cdc_locator_set_credentials(client_id, client_token, install = FALSE)

Arguments

client_id

Your Locator API client ID, a single string.

client_token

Your Locator API client token, a single string.

install

FALSE, the default, sets the credentials for this session only and writes no file. TRUE also saves them in your .Renviron file, after asking.

Value

NULL, invisibly. Called for its side effects.

Details

With install = TRUE, the function first asks whether to save the credentials, naming the file, and writes only after you answer yes. It writes to the file named by the R_ENVIRON_USER environment variable if that is set, and otherwise to .Renviron in the home folder R uses at startup (on Windows, R_USER if set, then HOME). Any existing CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID and CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN lines are replaced, and every other line is kept. The file is made readable only by you before the credentials are written to it; if that isn't possible, nothing is saved. (On Windows, files are protected by the permissions of your home folder.) Because it must ask, install = TRUE only works in an interactive session.

R reads only one user .Renviron when it starts. If the folder you start R in (in RStudio, the project's folder) has its own .Renviron, R reads that file instead of the one in your home folder, so credentials saved there don't apply in that project. The function warns you when this is the case.

Avoid typing the token into a script you might share. Calling this function with values read from a password manager, or with rstudioapi::askForPassword(), keeps them out of your code.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# For this session only
cdc_locator_set_credentials(
  client_id = "your-client-id",
  client_token = "your-client-token"
)

# Also save them for future sessions, after confirming
cdc_locator_set_credentials(
  client_id = "your-client-id",
  client_token = "your-client-token",
  install = TRUE
)
} # }
